title: Yaa Asantewaa, Queen Mother of Ejisu
summary: Queen Mother of Ejisu in the Asante (Ashanti) confederacy, appointed by her brother in the 1880s. In 1900 she became a leader of the Asante resistance to British rule known as the War of the Golden Stool. She was captured, exiled to the Seychelles in 1901, and died there in 1921.

uncertainty.note: Birth year is not fixed: BlackPast says it is contested, generally placed between the 1840s and 1860s; 1850 is a midpoint. The death year 1921 is given by both sources.

as_recorded.value: mid-1800s-1921 (birthdate contested; generally believed born between the 1840s to 1860s)

where.modern_name: Ejisu, Ashanti Region, Ghana (seat of her queen-motherhood; she was born at Besease, a town south of Ejisu)
where.historical_name: Ejisu, a district of the Asante (Ashanti) confederacy

importance.justification: Leader of the 1900 Asante rising against British rule, and a lasting symbol of resistance in Ghana.

sources.title: October 17, 1921: Yaa Asantewaa, Queenmother of Ejisu dies in the Seychelles

reviewer_note: Least sure of the birth year (contested) and of the source mix: BlackPast is a reader-supported online encyclopedia and the second source is a museum foundation's blog, not a university or national archive. Britannica, the British Museum and Georgia State thesis leads were blocked. The pin is modern Ejisu town, not the exact palace or Besease birthplace.
